Rashi on Shabbat 144b:10:1.english: From the bale of the olive press - After its oil has been pressed, or before its pressing.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:11:1.hebrew: מאי בינייהו - במאי פליגי? הואיל ותרוייהו מודו דמוחל היוצא בתחילה טהור, והיוצא מעקל בית הבד טמא, באיזה מוחל נחלקו, דלמר הוי משקה וטמא ולמר לא הוי משקה וטהור:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:11:1.english: What is [the difference] between them - In what do they disagree? Since both of them agree that olive discharge that emerges at the beginning is [ritually] pure, and that which emerges from the bale of the olive press is [ritually] impure, over which olive discharge did they disagree, such that according to one master it is [considered] a liquid and is impure, and according to the other master it is not [considered] a liquid and is pure?

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:11:2.hebrew: דאתי בתר איצצתא - לאחר שהתחילו להתחמם ודחקו זה את זה, ונשתהה הכומר ימים:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:11:2.english: That comes after pressing - After [the olives] began to warm up and pressed against one another, and the heap [of olives] remained for days.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:11:3.hebrew: רבא אמר - קמייתא דקתני מוחל פוסל מקוה, דברי הכל הוא, ומשום דהוי כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:11:3.english: Rava said - The first [teaching] that teaches [that] olive discharge invalidates a mikveh is [according to] everyone, and [it is] because it is, etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:12:1.hebrew: לתוך הקדרה - של תבשיל, לתקנו, דמוכחא מילתא דלאו למשקה בעי ליה אלא לאוכל, ואין זה דרך פריקתו, והוי כמפריד אוכל מאוכל:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:12:1.english: Into the pot - of cooked food, to improve it, for it is evident that he does not want it for a beverage, but rather for food; and this is not its [normal] manner of extraction, and it is like separating food from food.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:12:2.hebrew: אבל לא לתוך הקערה - דזמנין דלמשקה קאי, ואף על גב דבקערה לא שתי איניש, לא מוכחא מילתא ואיכא איסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:12:2.english: However, not into a bowl - For sometimes it is intended as a beverage; and even though a person does not drink from a bowl, the matter is not evident [that it is for food], and there is a prohibition.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:12:3.hebrew: אלמא - מדקאמר סוחט לתוך הקדרה, קסבר כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:12:3.english: Apparently - Since he says, "one may squeeze into the pot," he holds, etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:13:1.hebrew: החלב טמא - שהזב מטמא כל דבר במשא, והרי היסט הקילוח, ולא קמפליג בין לתוך הקדרה בין לתוך הכוס:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:13:1.english: The milk is ritually impure - For a zav renders anything ritually impure through carrying, and here [there is] movement of the stream [of milk], and [the Mishnah] does not distinguish between [milking] into a pot and [milking] into a cup.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:13:2.hebrew: ואי אמרת אוכל הוא - הא אין אוכל מקבל טומאה שלא בהכשר, והאי במאי איתכשר:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:13:2.english: And if you say it is food - Behold, food does not contract ritual impurity without being rendered susceptible, and with what was this [milk] rendered susceptible?

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:14:1.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said - In Tractate Keritot, regarding the woman from whose breasts milk dripped.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:14:2.hebrew: בטיפה המלוכלכת על פי הדד - טיפה ראשונה מלכלכת בה פי הדד בדעת, ונוחה ליחלב, וההיא הוי משקה כסתם חלב, דלא לאוכל בעי ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:14:2.english: With the drop that is smeared on the top of the teat - [With the] first drop, one smears the top of the teat with it intentionally so that it is easy to milk, and that [drop] is [considered] a liquid like ordinary milk, for he does not want it for food.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:1:1.hebrew: בפגעין - פרונ"ש בלע"ז, ולהוציא מימיהן לשתות:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:1:1.english: With plums - prunes in the vernacular [Old French], and [one squeezes them] to extract their juice to drink.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:1:3.hebrew: ובעוזרדין - קורמ"ש, דלאו אורחייהו בהכי, ואין כאן משום דש:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:1:3.english: And with crab apples - [In Old French:] cormes [sorb apples], for it is not their usual manner [to be squeezed] in this way, and there is no [prohibition] here on account of threshing.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:1:4.english: However, not with pomegranates - For it is their way [to be squeezed] thus.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:1:5.hebrew: ושל בית מנשיא - היו רגילין לסחוט רמונים בחול, אלמא איכא דסחיט להו. הלכך, בשבת אסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:1:5.english: And [those] of the house of Menashya - They were accustomed to squeeze pomegranates on a weekday; thus, there are [people] who squeeze them. Therefore, on Shabbat it is forbidden.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:2:1.hebrew: אלא מאי אית לך למימר - לר' יהודה: כיון דלאו בני סחיטה כו'. וכי היכי דלרבי יהודה שרי לכתחילה מהאי טעמא, מהשתא אפי' תימא רבנן ושרו ליה מהאי טעמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:2:1.english: Rather, what have you to say - According to Rabbi Yehuda: "Since they are not [fruits] designated for squeezing," etc. And just as according to Rabbi Yehuda it is permitted ab initio for this reason, now [you can] even say [it is] the Rabbis, and they permit it for this reason.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:4:1.hebrew: מנשיא תנא הוא - בתמיה, וכי איהו פליג למימר דבשבת אסור דתימא הלכתא כוותיה? והא לא הוזכר אלא לדברי התנא לראיה, דהאי תנא הוא סבר כוותיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:4:1.english: Is Menashya a tanna - [This is asked] in astonishment: did he himself disagree [with anyone] to say that on Shabbat it is forbidden, that you should say the halakha is in accordance with him? Why, he was only mentioned in the words of the tanna as a proof, [namely,] that this tanna holds in accordance with him.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:4:2.hebrew: וכ"ת - הא דאמר הלכה כשל בית מנשיא, ה"ק: הלכה כהאי תנא דאסר ברימונים, הואיל וקאי מנשיא כוותיה דסוחטין רימונים בחול, אלמא בני סחיטה נינהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:4:2.english: And if you say - [Regarding] that which he said, "The halakha is in accordance with [the practice of] the house of Menashya," this is what he is saying: The halakha is in accordance with that Tanna who prohibits [squeezing] pomegranates, since Menashya agrees with him, as they squeeze pomegranates on a weekday; thus, they are [considered] subject to squeezing.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:4:3.english: [Does he] constitute the majority of the world - That because of him alone we should make the [normal] way of pomegranates [to be] for squeezing?

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:5:2.hebrew: מקדש - את התבואה משום כלאים, דזריעה הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:5:2.english: Renders forbidden - [He renders] the grain [forbidden] because of diverse kinds [kilayim], for it is [considered] sowing.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:5:3.english: And Rabbi Chanina said, etc. - Thus, because of one place that considered them significant, we treat them as a significant thing.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:6:1.hebrew: אתרא - הוא, וחשיבות דרבים הוי חשיבותא:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:6:1.english: A place - It is, and the significance of the many is [considered] significance.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:6:2.hebrew: הכא - חד גברא לחודיה הוא, נימא בטלה דעתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:6:2.english: Here - He is one man alone, [so] we say his opinion is nullified.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:7:1.english: Rather, this is the reason - [for the statement] of Rav Nachman, who said [that] the halakha is [that] one may not squeeze [pomegranates].

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:7:2.hebrew: כרב חסדא - אע"ג דלעלמא לא חשיב, כיון דאחשיב איהו, הוי לדידיה משקה. והכי מפרש רב נחמן לברייתא דלעיל: "סוחטין בפגעין ובפרישין" — למתק הפרי, ולא לצורך המשקה — "אבל לא ברימונים" — ואפילו למתקן, דשל בית מנשיא היו סוחטין בחול לצורך משקה. הלכך, בשבת אסור אפי' למתק, הואיל ואיכא חד דעביד לשם משקה. ולא משום דמנשיא רובא דעלמא, אלא חיישינן אי שרית ליה למתק, אתי למעבד לשום משקה, וכיון דאיהו מחשב ליה, הוי משקה ומיחייב. אבל בפגעין ליכא למיחש, דאין אדם עושה אותו למשקה:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:7:2.english: In accordance with [the opinion of] Rav Chisda - Even though to the general public it is not considered significant, since he [himself] ascribed it significance, it is [considered] a liquid for him. And thus Rav Nachman explains the baraita above: "One may squeeze plums and quinces" — to sweeten the fruit, and not for the sake of the liquid — "but not pomegranates" — even to sweeten them, since those of the house of Menashya would squeeze [them] on weekdays for the sake of [their] liquid. Therefore, on Shabbat it is forbidden even to sweeten [them], since there is one [person] who does [so] for the sake of [extracting] a liquid. And [this is] not because [the house of] Menashya [represents] the majority of the world, but rather we are concerned [that] if you permit him to sweeten [them], he will come to do [so] for the sake of [extracting] a liquid, and since he considers it [a liquid], it becomes a liquid and he is liable. However, with regard to plums, there is no reason to be concerned, for no person makes it into a liquid.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:7:3.hebrew: בשינוי מראה - לא בשלשת לוגין, דלא הוזכרו שלש לוגין אלא במים שאובין, אבל שאר משקין לא פסלי אא"כ נשתנה מראה המקוה על ידיהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:7:3.english: Through a change of appearance - Not with three lugin, for three lugin were mentioned only with regard to drawn water, whereas other liquids do not invalidate [the mikveh] unless the appearance of the mikveh was changed by them.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:8:1.hebrew: רב פפא אמר - טעמא דתרדין לאו משום חשיבותא דאחשבינהו הוא, ולעולם לאו משקה נינהו. והא דמפסיל, משום דכל דבר שאין עושין ממנו מקוה — שאינו מים או שלג או ברד — פוסל את המקוה בשינוי מראה:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:8:1.english: Rav Pappa said - The reason [for the ruling regarding] beets is not because of [their] significance, that he deemed them [a liquid], and in fact they are not [considered] a liquid. And the reason it invalidates [the ritual bath] is because anything with which one does not make a ritual bath — [that is, anything] that is not water, snow, or hail — invalidates the ritual bath through a change of appearance.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:9:1.hebrew: נפל לתוכו - של מקוה, יין או חומץ או מוחל. והוא כמין מים וזב מן הזיתים, וג' מינים יש בו: כשטוענן מתחילה במעטן להתחמם ולהתבשל מאיליהן, מוחל זב מהן והוא צלול כמים; ולאחר שעמדו ימים ודחקו זה את זה, חוזר מוחל לזוב מהן והוא קרוב להיות כשמן; ולאחר שעצרן להוציא שמנן בבית הבד, ומשתהה התפוח של גפת בעקלים שהוא אגוד בהן בבית הבד, חוזר מוחל וזב מהן:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:9:1.english: Fell into it - [Into] a mikveh, [there fell] wine or vinegar or mohal [olive discharge]. It is a kind of water that flows from olives, and there are three kinds of it: when one initially loads [the olives] into the vat to warm up and ripen on their own, mohal flows from them, and it is clear like water; and after they have stood for days and pressed against one another, mohal again flows from them, and it is close to being like oil; and after one has pressed them to extract their oil in the olive press, and the heap of olive pomace remains in the pressing baskets in which it is bound in the olive press, mohal again flows from them.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:9:2.hebrew: מאן תנא דמוחל משקה הוא - קס"ד דאין מקוה נפסל אלא על ידי משקה, ואפילו בשינוי מראה:
Rashi on Shabbat 144b:9:2.english: Who is the Tanna [who holds] that [olive] discharge is a liquid - [The Gemara] initially assumed that a mikveh is invalidated only by a liquid, even [when invalidated] through a change in appearance.

Rashi on Shabbat 144b:9:3.english: At the outset - At the beginning of loading the olives [into the press].

Tosafot on Shabbat 144b:12:1.hebrew: חולב אדם עז כו' - נראה לר"ת דהיינו דווקא בי"ט, דחזיא בהמה לאכילה, הוי כמו אוכלא דאיפרת; אבל בשבת לא חזיא לשחיטה, כמו דש חשיבא, שהבהמה היא כפסולת, וכשחולב הוי כנוטל אוכל מתוך פסולת. וכן משמע בבה"ג דבי"ט איירי. ומיהו סחיטת זיתים וענבים דשרי לעיל לתוך הקדירה, היינו אפי' בשבת, כיון דאשכול חזיא לאכילה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 144b:12:1.english: "One may milk a goat, etc." - It appears to Rabbeinu Tam that this [ruling] applies specifically on Yom Tov, [for] since the animal is fit for eating, it is like food that separated [from food]; however, on Shabbat it is not fit for slaughter, [so milking] is considered like threshing, for the animal is like refuse, and when one milks [it], it is like taking food out of refuse. And so it is implied in Ba'al Halakhot Gedolot that [the Gemara] is speaking of Yom Tov. However, squeezing olives and grapes, which [the Gemara] permitted above [to squeeze] into a pot, that [applies] even on Shabbat, since a cluster [of grapes] is fit for eating.

Tosafot on Shabbat 144b:6:1.hebrew: מי דמי ערביא אתרא הוא - הו"מ למיפרך: הניחא לרבי אליעזר, לרבנן מאי איכא למימר? אלא פריך דאפילו לרבי אליעזר לא ניחא. ומה שקשה מאנשי הוצל דפרק המצניע (לעיל שבת דף צב:), פירשתי שם (ד"ה ואת"ל):
Tosafot on Shabbat 144b:6:1.english: Is it comparable? Arabia is a place - [The Gemara] could have objected: That works out well according to Rabbi Eliezer, [but] according to the Rabbis, what is there to say? Rather, it objects that even according to Rabbi Eliezer it is not satisfactory. And as for what is difficult from the people of Hutzal in the chapter Hamatzni'a (above, Shabbat 92b), I have explained [it] there (s.v. Ve'im Timtzei Lomar).

Tosafot on Shabbat 144b:7:1.hebrew: ה"נ כיון דאחשביה הווה להו משקה - תחילה ס"ד ד"סוחטין בפגעין כו'" היינו סחיטה ממש, אבל השתא אי אפשר לומר, דהא פשיטא דאסור, דכיון דאחשביה הוה להו משקה; אלא "סוחטין" דקתני, היינו בליציי"ר בלע"ז — למתק הפרי, כדפי' בקונטרס:
Tosafot on Shabbat 144b:7:1.english: Here, too, since he ascribed it significance, it is [considered] a liquid - Initially, we thought that "One may squeeze unripe figs, etc." meant actual squeezing, but now it is impossible to say [so], for it is obvious that [actual squeezing] is forbidden, since once he ascribed significance to it, it becomes a liquid. Rather, "one may squeeze" that [the Baraita] teaches means blecier in Old French [i.e., bruising/softening] to sweeten the fruit, as [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres.

Tosafot on Shabbat 144b:9:1.hebrew: אמר אביי ר' יעקב היא - קשה לי: לימא דהאי מוחל דקתני היינו במוחל היוצא מעקול בית הבד, ודברי הכל! וכי תימא: מדקתני מוחל סתמא, משמע דבכל מוחל איירי — לא היא, דע"כ אפי' לרבי יעקב לא איירי בכל מוחל, דהא מודה דמוחל היוצא בתחילה טהור. י"ל: דמוחל היוצא מעקול בית הבד לא הוה קרינן ליה "מוחל" סתם, כיון דאי אפשר לו בלא צחצוחי שמן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 144b:9:1.english: Abaye said: It is Rabbi Yaakov - It is difficult for me: why not say that this [olive] discharge that [the Mishnah] teaches refers to [olive] discharge that emerges from the bale of the olive press, and [thus] it is the opinion of all [even Rabbi Shimon]? And if you will say: since [the Mishnah] teaches "[olive] discharge" without qualification, it implies that it is speaking of all [types of olive] discharge — that is not so! For perforce, even according to Rabbi Yaakov, it is not speaking of all [types of olive] discharge, since he concedes that [olive] discharge that emerges at the outset is ritually pure. One can answer: we would not have called [olive] discharge that emerges from the bale of the olive press simply "[olive] discharge" without qualification, since it is impossible for it [to be] without drops of oil.
